questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A newspaper published an editorial in which an editor asserted that a candidate for high political office was a user of illegal drugs. The accusation was untrue. The editor acted unreasonably in not investigating the accusation before publishing it; however, the editor honestly believed that the accusation was true.
The candidate sued the editor for defamation.
Is the candidate entitled to recover?

choices.A: No, because the accusation appeared in an editorial and was therefore merely an opinion.
choices.B: No, because the editor honestly believed that the accusation was true.
choices.C: Yes, because calling someone an illegal drug user is defamatory per se.
choices.D: Yes, because the accusation was false and injurious to the candidate's reputation.

questions.explanation:
Defamation
(defendant's culpability when making a false statement)
Who is the plaintiff?
↓
Private person
(most plaintiffs)
Public figure
(eg. celebrity, social activist)
Public official
(eg. congressperson, governor)
↓
Defendant must act with
• knowledge that statement is false
OR
• negligent disregard for its falsity
↓
Defendant must act with actual malice
• knowledge that statement is false
OR
• reckless disregard for its falsity

Defamation can be either slander (spoken statements) OR libel (written statements—as here). A defamation claim based on libel ordinarily requires proof that:

  • the defendant knowingly made a false statement about the plaintiff or negligently failed to determine its falsity
  • that type of statement would tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation and
  • the defendant intentionally or negligently communicated that statement to a third party.

But when the plaintiff is a public figure or official (eg. celebrity, governor), he/she must prove that the false statement was made with actual malice. Actual malice exists where the defendant knew that the statement was false or recklessly disregarded its falsity (ie, had serious doubts about its truthfulness). Therefore, proof of negligence—failure to use reasonable care to determine a statement's falsity—is not enough.

Here, the editor falsely accused the candidate of using illegal drugs in a published editorial. Since the candidate is a public figure, he can only recover for defamation if the editor acted with actual malice. And since the editor honestly believed that the accusation was true (not actual malice), the candidate cannot recover for defamation.

(Choice B) Defamation can stem from a statement alleging a fact or an opinion that appears to be based on specific facts. Here, the editorial asserted that the candidate used illegal drugs (factual allegation). But a stated belief about the candidate's drug use (opinion) would still be actionable if it implied knowledge of specific facts.

(Choice C) Statements that are presumptively harmful to the plaintiff's reputation are considered defamatory per se. Though accusing someone of a criminal act (illegal drug use) is defamatory per se, the candidate will not prevail because the editor believed that the accusation was true (no actual malice).

(Choice D) Although the editor's accusation was false and likely injurious to the candidate's reputation, the candidate will not prevail because the editor did not act with actual malice.

📌 Educational Objective

A public figure or public official can only recover for defamation if he/she proves that the defendant made a false statement with actual malice, ie, with knowledge or reckless disregard of the statement's falsity.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 558 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (elements of defamation).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 568 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (libel and slander distinguished).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 580A (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (defamation of public official or public figure).

一家报纸发表了一篇社论，其中一位编辑断言，一位高级政治职位的候选人是非法药物使用者。该指控不属实。该编辑在发表前未对指控进行调查，其行为不合理；然而，该编辑真诚地相信该指控是真实的。

该候选人以诽谤为由起诉了该编辑。

该候选人是否有权获得赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为该指控出现在社论中，因此仅仅是一种意见。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为该编辑真诚地相信该指控是真实的。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为称某人为非法药物使用者构成本身即是诽谤 (defamatory per se)。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为该指控是虚假的，并且损害了候选人的声誉。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Other Torts - Defamation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：公众人物（public figure）提起诽谤（defamation）时，必须证明被告有实际恶意（actual malice），光有“没调查清楚”还不够。

三秒认题路径：

公众人物 → 虚假指控 → 真实相信 → 不是恶意 → 不能赔

核心法律规则

先看原告是谁：如果是公众人物（public figure）或公职人员（public official），他要赢诽谤（defamation），不能只证明被告疏忽（negligence），而要证明被告明知为假，或对真假鲁莽漠视（reckless disregard）。这里的实际恶意（actual malice）不是“态度很坏”，而是“知道不真还发，或者心里对真假有严重怀疑还照发”。

所以这题的关键不是“文章写在社论里”或“内容是否伤名誉”，而是编辑是否带着这种主观恶意去发。题干明说他真诚相信指控是真的，哪怕他调查不充分，也过不了公众人物诽谤的门槛。

核心判例： New York Times v. Sullivan — 公众人物/公职人员要赢诽谤，必须证明被告对虚假性有实际恶意。

思维导图

原告是谁？
YES：公众人物 / 公职人员
要证明什么？
虚假陈述 + 实际恶意（actual malice）
卡死点：只是不调查、只是不合理 ≠ 实际恶意
本题：编辑真诚相信是真的 → 没过实际恶意 → 不能胜诉
NO：普通私人
通常只要证明过失（negligence）即可，但这不是本题路径。
最终结论
选 B：没有实际恶意，就算陈述虚假也不赔。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这句话伤害名誉，又写成了“非法吸毒”，看起来当然该赔。

但考试真正问的是：公众人物能不能证明被告有实际恶意（actual malice），不是内容是不是很难听。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「名誉有没有被骂得很惨」。

另外，defamatory per se 只是在“损害名誉”这一步更容易成立，不会自动把“实际恶意”这个门槛抹掉。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干明确写编辑真诚相信指控为真，这就不是实际恶意（actual malice）；公众人物诽谤必须过这道门，故不能赔。

❌ 概念混淆 | 意见事实混淆

✕ A: 把 editorial 直接当意见，忽略了这其实是在陈述可验证事实。

❌ 法律适用 | per se 误放大

✕ C: 以为 defamatory per se 一出现就自动赢，忘了公众人物还要证实际恶意。

❌ 事实误判 | 漏掉主观要件

✕ D: 只盯着“虚假又伤人”，却漏看题干里最关键的恶意门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定原告身份，再查实际恶意；公职/公众人物题先问主观门槛，不先被名誉伤害带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：公众人物（public figure）打诽谤（defamation），先问有没有实际恶意（actual malice）；只是不调查、只是粗心，一般不够。

速记：New York Times v. Sullivan = “公众人物要赢，得抓到被告明知是假或严重怀疑还发”。

question_analysis.skill_tested: apply actual malice to public figures

reason.en: Triggers the heightened actual malice standard instead of ordinary negligence.
reason.zh: 触发更高的实际恶意标准，而非普通过失标准。

reason.en: Falsity alone is insufficient without proof of actual malice here.
reason.zh: 仅有虚假性不足以胜诉，还须证明实际恶意。

keywords.text: acted unreasonably in not investigating the accusation before publishing it

reason.en: Shows negligence, but negligence does not satisfy actual malice for a public figure.
reason.zh: 表明存在过失，但对公众人物而言过失不等于实际恶意。

keywords.text: honestly believed that the accusation was true

reason.en: Negates actual malice because the editor lacked knowledge or reckless disregard of falsity.
reason.zh: 表明被告无明知或鲁莽漠视虚假，从而否定实际恶意。

reason.en: Identifies libel in written form, though format alone does not defeat liability.
reason.zh: 表明以书面形式诽谤，但发表形式本身不能免责。

reason.en: Frames the cause of action whose elements depend on plaintiff status.
reason.zh: 界定诉讼请求，其构成要件因原告身份而不同。

reason.en: Mischaracterizes a factual drug-use accusation as nonactionable opinion.
reason.zh: 将事实性吸毒指控误当作不可诉的意见。

B.text: honestly believed that the accusation was true

reason.en: Correctly identifies the missing culpability element for a public figure plaintiff.
reason.zh: 正确指出公众人物原告所缺的过错要件。

reason.en: Invokes presumptive harm but ignores the actual malice requirement.
reason.zh: 援引当然损害推定，却忽略实际恶意要件。

D.text: false and injurious to the candidate's reputation

reason.en: States basic elements while omitting actual malice for a public figure.
reason.zh: 只列基本要件，遗漏公众人物须证明的实际恶意。

highlights.text: candidate for high political office

reason.en: Determines that recovery requires proof of actual malice, not mere negligence.
reason.zh: 决定原告须证明实际恶意，而非仅证明过失。

highlights.text: acted unreasonably in not investigating the accusation before publishing it

reason.en: Tempts selection of a negligence-based answer even though it is legally insufficient here.
reason.zh: 易诱使考生选择以过失为基础的错误选项，但此处不足够。

highlights.text: honestly believed that the accusation was true

reason.en: This belief defeats actual malice and therefore bars recovery.
reason.zh: 该真诚相信否定实际恶意，因而不能获得赔偿。

highlights.text: The accusation was untrue.

reason.en: Necessary for defamation but not sufficient without culpable state of mind.
reason.zh: 构成诽谤的必要条件，但无相应过错心态仍不足够。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A homeowner owns a house on a lake. A neighbor owns a house across a driveway from the homeowner's property. The neighbor's house sits on a hill, and the neighbor can see the lake from his living room window. The homeowner and the neighbor got into an argument, and the homeowner erected a large spotlight on his property that automatically comes on at dusk and goes off at sunrise. The only reason the homeowner installed the light was to annoy the neighbor. The glare from the light severely detracts from the neighbor's view of the lake.
In a suit by the neighbor against the homeowner, will the neighbor prevail?

choices.A: No, because the neighbor's view of the lake is not always obstructed.
choices.B: No, if the spotlight provides added security to the homeowner's property.
choices.C: Yes, because the homeowner installed the light solely to annoy the neighbor.
choices.D: Yes, if, and only if, the neighbor's property value is adversely affected.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Unreasonable interference for private nuisance
Per se nuisance• Defendant's conduct, in & of itself, is a nuisance
Conduct unsuited
to location		• Defendant's conduct is unsuited to location and
• Plaintiff's use & enjoyment of property are suited to location
Avoidable harm• Defendant's failure to exercise reasonable care regarding risk of harm caused interference
Severe harm• Plaintiff's land or fixtures sustained physical damage
Malicious conduct• Defendant's activity or condition created by defendant is motivated entirely or almost entirely by malice

When a person interferes with the plaintiff's use and enjoyment of his/her property, the plaintiff can sue for private nuisance. To prevail in that suit, the plaintiff must prove that the interference was both:

  • substantial – offensive, annoying, or intolerable to a normal person in the community and
  • unreasonable – effectively renders the land unavailable for ordinary use or enjoyment by the possessor and satisfies certain criteria (see table above).

Interference motivated entirely or almost entirely by malice—i.e., the defendant's sole purpose was to harm the plaintiff—is unreasonable as a matter of law because it has no legal utility (i.e., no social value).

Here, the homeowner substantially interfered with the neighbor's use and enjoyment of his property by installing a spotlight that severely detracted from his view of the lake each night. And since the spotlight was installed solely to annoy the neighbor (malice), that interference was unreasonable as a matter of law (no utility). Therefore, the neighbor will likely prevail in a private nuisance claim.

(Choice A) While evidence that an interference is continuous may prove that the interference is substantial and unreasonable, such evidence is not always required. Therefore, though his view of the lake was not always obstructed, the neighbor can prevail since the spotlight was a substantial and unreasonable interference.

(Choice B) Although the spotlight may add security to the homeowner's property (utility), the homeowner installed it for the sole purpose of annoying the neighbor—not for added security. Therefore, the interference was unreasonable as a matter of law and the neighbor will prevail.

(Choice D) Private nuisance does not require proof that the plaintiff's property value decreased. Instead, the neighbor will prevail because the spotlight substantially interfered with his use and enjoyment of his property and the homeowner installed it solely to annoy him.

📌 Educational Objective

Private nuisance is a substantial and unreasonable interference with the plaintiff's use and enjoyment of his/her property. An interference is unreasonable if it effectively renders the land unavailable for ordinary use or enjoyment and satisfies certain criteria —e.g., when the interference was motivated entirely or almost entirely by malice.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 821D, 822 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (liability for private nuisance).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 826 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (unreasonableness requirement).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 829 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (malicious or indecent conduct).
questions.zh-question:
一位房主在湖边拥有一所房屋。一位邻居的房屋与该房主的房产隔着一条车道。邻居的房屋坐落在一座小山上，邻居可以从他家的客厅窗户看到湖景。房主与邻居发生了争执，于是房主在其房产上安装了一个大型聚光灯，该灯在黄昏时自动开启，在日出时自动关闭。房主安装此灯的唯一原因是为了骚扰邻居。灯光的强光严重影响了邻居对湖景的欣赏。

在邻居对房主提起的诉讼中，邻居会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为邻居的湖景并非一直被遮挡。
zh-choices.B: 不会，如果该聚光灯为房主的财产提供了额外的安全保障。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为房主安装此灯的唯一目的是为了骚扰邻居。
zh-choices.D: 会，当且仅当邻居的房产价值受到不利影响时。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Other Torts - Nuisance

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：私人妨害（private nuisance）里，故意为恶意骚扰而设置的灯光会不会被直接认定为“不合理干扰”。

三秒认题路径：

邻居干扰 → 私人妨害 → 恶意动机 → 不合理 → 选 C

核心法律规则

私人妨害（private nuisance）考的是：被告对原告使用与享有（use and enjoyment）的房产造成了重大且不合理（substantial and unreasonable）的干扰。考试里，重大就是让正常人觉得烦、刺眼、难受；不合理就是让土地几乎不能正常使用。

如果被告的行为几乎完全出于恶意（malice），也就是只想害对方，没有社会效用，考试上会直接把这类干扰当成不合理。对这题来说，关键不是灯有没有别的用途，而是房主承认唯一目的就是惹恼邻居。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts §§ 821D, 822, 826, 829 —— 恶意驱动的干扰缺乏合法效用，所以可直接认定为不合理。

思维导图

看到邻居告你 private nuisance，先问：干扰是不是 substantial ＋ unreasonable？
第 1 步：灯光每晚都刺眼、严重影响看湖景 → 干扰是重大。
第 2 步：安装原因不是安全，而是solely to annoy → 直接打上 不合理 = 恶意目的，没有社会效用
第 3 步：即使没有把湖景“永久遮住”，也不影响结论；effectively reviewable 不是这里的标准，本题看的是干扰是否足够恶意、足够不合理。
结论：原告可赢，答案落在 Yes，因为被告只想惹恼邻居。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：灯光只是让视线变差，并没有一直把湖挡住，所以原告不一定能赢。

但考试真正问的是：这类干扰是否已经够重大且不合理，而不是它有没有“全天候完全遮挡”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 solely to annoy the neighbor 直接把行为推成恶意干扰；私人妨害里，这种只为伤人的灯光会被当成不合理，原告可赢。

❌ 事实误判 | 全天遮挡偷换

✕ A: 把not always obstructed当成关键，偷换成“必须全天遮挡”。

❌ 法律适用 | 安全效用误套

✕ B: 看到added security就想当然，但题干说房主只是想惹人，不是为了安全。

❌ 概念混淆 | 价值下降误当要件

✕ D: 把property value当成必考点，但私人妨害看的是使用和享有受扰，不要求先证明贬值。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“恶意目的”这条硬事实，再用私人妨害的“不合理”要件直接锁答案。

考场速记

记住一句：私人妨害先看“有没有严重干扰”，再看“这个干扰合不合理”；只为报复的行为，通常直接判不合理。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A lawyer conducted a free consultation with a businessman who wanted advice on a tax matter for which he sought a refund from the IRS. The lawyer declined to represent the businessman, but an eager intern who had overheard their conversation stopped the businessman as he was leaving the office. The intern told the businessman that she was a law student and wanted to share her opinion with him. She then told the businessman that she believed that the applicable statute of limitations for claiming a refund had more than a year to run and that he had plenty of time in which to act before his legal rights would expire.
Although the intern believed this statement to be accurate, the statute of limitations for claiming a refund had only days to run at the time of the consultation. Relying on the intern's statement, the businessman delayed in contacting another attorney to assist him with the tax refund claim. As a result, his refund claim was barred by the statute of limitations.
The businessman has sued the intern for negligent misrepresentation, seeking damages for financial loss resulting from his inability to timely file for a refund. The intern has filed a motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim.
How should the court rule on the intern's motion?

choices.A: Deny it, because the businessman is seeking to recover only pecuniary damages and not damages for physical harm.
choices.B: Deny it, because the intern should have known that her statement about the statute of limitations was false.
choices.C: Grant it, because the intern believed that the statute of limitations had more than a year to run when she made that statement.
choices.D: Grant it, because the intern was expressing a lay opinion that the businessman should not have relied upon.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Misrepresentation
(fraudulent v. negligent)
ConductSettingHarm
FraudulentKnowingly or recklessly misrepresented material fact to induce relianceAny settingJustifiable reliance caused
• pecuniary loss
NegligentNegligently provided plaintiff false informationCommercial setting or setting with risk of physical harmJustifiable reliance caused
• pecuniary loss or
• physical harm

Negligent misrepresentation is based upon a breach of the duty to supply correct information and often arises in the context of accountants and other suppliers of commercial information (eg, attorneys).

This tort requires proof of the following elements:

  • The defendant negligently provided false information during the course of his/her business or profession.
  • The plaintiff justifiably relied upon the false information and suffered pecuniary (ie, financial) loss as a result (Choice A).
  • The plaintiff was in a contractual relationship with the defendant or was a third party known by the defendant as one for whose benefit the information was supplied.

A plaintiff's reliance was not justified if the information was obviously false or if the defendant was clearly stating a lay opinion.

Here, the intern provided the businessman with false information regarding the statute of limitations. However, she was clearly expressing a lay opinion since she told the businessman that she was still a law student and merely offering an opinion. As a result, the businessman cannot establish that he justifiably relied upon the information provided, and the intern's motion to dismiss should be granted (Choice D).

*Additionally, there was no contractual relationship between the businessman and the intern, so the businessman also cannot establish that element of negligent misrepresentation.

(Choice C) Negligent misrepresentation requires that the defendant act negligently. Negligence will be found if the defendant failed to exercise the same level of care and competence as a reasonable person in his/her business or professional position. The standard is an objective one, so the intern's subjective belief that her statement was true is irrelevant.

📌 Educational Objective

One of the elements of negligent misrepresentation is that the plaintiff's reliance on the false information provided was justifiable. Reliance was not justified if the information was obviously false or the defendant was clearly stating a lay opinion.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 552 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (negligent misrepresentation).
questions.zh-question:
一名律师为一位商人提供了免费咨询，该商人就一桩税务事宜寻求建议，他希望就此事从美国国税局（IRS）获得退税。律师拒绝代理该商人，但一名热切的实习生无意中听到了他们的谈话，在该商人离开办公室时叫住了他。实习生告诉该商人她是一名法学生，并想与他分享自己的看法。随后，她告诉该商人，她认为申请退税的诉讼时效尚有一年多才到期，他有充足的时间在法律权利失效前采取行动。

尽管该实习生相信这一陈述是准确的，但在咨询当时，申请退税的诉讼时效仅剩数天。该商人信赖了实习生的陈述，延迟了联系另一位律师协助他处理退税申请。结果，他的退税申请因诉讼时效届满而被禁止。

该商人以过失性失实陈述为由起诉了该实习生，要求赔偿因未能及时申请退税而造成的经济损失。实习生以未能陈述有效诉由为由，提出了驳回起诉的动议。

法院应如何裁定实习生的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该动议，因为该商人仅寻求追偿金钱损失，而非人身伤害赔偿。
zh-choices.B: 驳回该动议，因为该实习生本应知道她关于诉讼时效的陈述是错误的。
zh-choices.C: 批准该动议，因为实习生在作出该陈述时，相信诉讼时效尚有一年多。
zh-choices.D: 批准该动议，因为实习生表达的是一种非专业意见，该商人本不应信赖。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Other Torts - Negligent misrepresentation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：过失性错误陈述（negligent misrepresentation）里，受害人能不能说自己对一个明显只是排除性意见（lay opinion）的说法作了“合理依赖”。

三秒认题路径：

错误信息 → 合理依赖 → 只是意见 → 不可依赖 → 直接驳回

核心法律规则

过失性错误陈述（negligent misrepresentation）要求：被告在其业务或职业中提供了错误信息，原告对该信息作了正当依赖（justifiable reliance），并因此发生了金钱损失（pecuniary loss）。但如果信息只是被告明确表示的排除性意见（lay opinion），考试上通常就不能算可依赖的信息。

这里的关键不是她心里“以为自己说对了”，而是她当场告诉对方自己只是法学生、只是在给意见，所以这句话更像建议，不像专业结论。正当依赖（justifiable reliance）这一关过不了，诉讼就会被挡在门外。

核心判例：Restatement (Second) of Torts § 552 — 这类问题专看“提供信息的人是否在业务/职业中说错了、对方是否合理依赖了”。

思维导图

1. 信息来源
被告在咨询中给了一个关于报税时限的具体说法，属于信息提供。
2. 职业场景
律师办公室里给建议，形式上接近专业信息，但她并未以执业者身份承诺结论。
3. 依赖是否正当
她先说自己只是法学生，等于把话标成意见，听的人不该把它当可放心下注的专业判断。
4. 损失结果
原告因拖延而错过退款期限，出现了金钱损失。
5. 结论闸门
不正当依赖 这一项断掉，negligent misrepresentation 直接失败。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她说错了时限，原告又真的吃亏了，应该能告。

但考试真正问的是：对方有没有把这句话当成专业信息来信，而不是一个法学生现场给的lay opinion。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以这里不是先盯着损失有多惨，而是先卡住“这话值不值得信”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干先声明自己只是法学生、只是给意见，这让对方对时限说法的依赖不再正当，所以 negligent misrepresentation 不能成立。

❌ 事实误判 | 只看损失

✕ A: 只盯着pecuniary damages，却漏了依赖必须正当。

❌ 法律适用 | 主观善意误判

✕ B: 把“她真心相信”当护身符，考试不看主观善意。

❌ 概念混淆 | 故意过错混进来

✕ C: 误把believed true当成免责点，和本题的依赖问题不是一回事。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看说话人有没有把信息降格成意见，再查原告能否正当依赖。

考场速记

记住一句：过失性错误陈述（negligent misrepresentation）先看“是不是专业信息”，再看“能不能合理信”。

见到对方明确说“我只是给意见”“我只是学生”，就先警惕lay opinion；一旦依赖不正当，题目通常直接结束。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man and a woman were law school classmates who had competed for the position of editor of the law review. The man had the higher grade point average, but the woman was elected editor, largely in recognition of a long and important note that had appeared in the review with the woman credited as the author.
During the following placement interview season, the man was interviewed by a representative of a nationally prominent law firm. In response to the interviewer's request for information about the authorship of the law review note, the man said that he believed that the note attributed to the woman was largely the work of another student.
The firm told the woman that it would not interview her because of doubts about the authorship of the note. This greatly distressed the woman. In fact, the note had been prepared by the woman without assistance from anyone else.
If the woman asserts a claim against the man based on defamation, will she recover?

choices.A: No, because the statement was made by the man only after the interviewer inquired about the authorship of the note.
choices.B: No, unless the woman proves pecuniary loss.
choices.C: Yes, because the man's statement was false.
choices.D: Yes, if the man had substantial doubts about the accuracy of the information he gave the interviewer.

questions.explanation:
Claim
Defamation
Defendant communicated false statement about plaintiff to third party and caused harm?
Yes
↓
Defense
Privilege
Defendant reasonably believed statement affected important interest of third party?
Yes
↓
Counterdefense
Privilege abused
Defendant knew statement was false or had substantial doubts about accuracy?
Yes
↓
Liable
→
No
Not Liable

Defamation (libel or slander) occurs when a defendant communicates (ie, publishes) a false statement about the plaintiff to a third party and harms the plaintiff's reputation. But the defendant is not liable for that communication if it is privileged. One such privilege arises when the defendant reasonably believes that:

  • the statement affects an important interest of the third party, and
  • communicating that statement to the third party is socially acceptable—eg, the statement is made in response to a request rather than volunteered.

However, this is a conditional privilege that is lost when abused. Abuse occurs when the defendant knows that the statement is false or recklessly disregards that possibility, ie, has substantial doubts about the statement's accuracy.

Here, the man falsely told the interviewer that the woman's law review note was largely the work of another student (the interviewer). This communication was privileged since (1) the man could reasonably believe that the statement would affect the interviewer's hiring decision (important interest) and (2) the statement was made in response to the interviewer's inquiry about the note (socially acceptable) (Choice A). But if the man had substantial doubts about the accuracy of his statement, then the privilege will be lost and the woman will recover for defamation.

(Choice B) Slander (spoken defamation) ordinarily requires proof of special harm (pecuniary loss). But such proof is not required when the defendant's statement constitutes slander per se—eg, a statement accusing the plaintiff of conduct that adversely affects his/her occupation. Here, since an accusation of plagiarism would harm a law student's job prospects (slander per se), the woman can recover without proving pecuniary loss.

(Choice C) Since defamation requires proof of falsity, the fact that the man's statement was false supports the woman's claim. But since the man's statement was privileged, the woman will only recover if this privilege was abused, ie, the man knew or recklessly disregarded the possibility that his statement was false.

(Choice D) The privilege is lost if the defendant had substantial doubts about the accuracy of the information he gave the interviewer, which would amount to reckless disregard and abuse of the privilege.

📌 Educational Objective

A defamation statement communicated to a third party is privileged when the defendant reasonably believes that (1) the statement affects an important interest of the third party and (2) the communication is socially acceptable. This privilege is lost if the defendant knows that the statement is false or recklessly disregards that possibility.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 558 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (elements of defamation)
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 595 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (statements made to protect third party's interest)
questions.zh-question:
一名男子和一名女子是法学院的同学，他们曾竞争《法律评论》的编辑职位。该男子的平均绩点更高，但该女子当选为编辑，主要是因为她在《法律评论》上发表了一篇署名为作者的重要长文，并因此获得了认可。

在接下来的求职面试季，该男子接受了一家全国知名律师事务所代表的面试。在回应面试官关于该法律评论文章作者身份的询问时，该男子称，他听说署名为该女子的文章，主要由另一名学生完成。

该律所告知该女子，由于对其文章作者身份存疑，将不会对她进行面试。这让该女子极为痛苦。事实上，该文章由该女子独立完成，没有任何人协助。

如果该女子以诽谤为由对该男子提起诉讼，她能否获得赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不能获得赔偿，除非该女子能证明有金钱损失。
zh-choices.B: 不能获得赔偿，因为该男子的陈述是在面试官询问文章作者身份后才作出的。
zh-choices.C: 能获得赔偿，因为该男子的陈述是虚假的。
zh-choices.D: 能获得赔偿，如果该男子对他提供给面试官的信息的准确性有重大怀疑。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Other Torts - Defamation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：诽谤（defamation）里，虽然话是假的，但如果是为第三人利益而作的特权通信（conditional privilege），就要再看有没有被滥用。

三秒认题路径：

对第三人说话 → 先看特权 → 再看滥用 → 有无reckless disregard → 选 D

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则

诽谤（defamation）要有对第三人的传播、虚假陈述和名誉损害；但如果说话人是为了保护第三人的重要利益，而且是在对方询问下作出陈述，就可能有条件特权（conditional privilege）。考试上这句人话的意思是：先别急着因为“说错了”就判输，先问这句话是不是本来就允许对第三人说。

这个特权不是免死金牌；如果说话人明知可能是假的，或者对真伪有substantial doubts，特权就会被滥用而失效。也就是：能不能免责，不看你“有没有把人害惨”，先看你当时是不是还在诚信地帮第三方说话。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 595 的思路锁定本题：为保护第三方利益的陈述，满足条件时有特权，但知道或严重怀疑其真实性时，特权会被打掉。

思维导图

先问：这是不是可以立刻按“说了假话”直接赔？
1.对第三人传播（publication）：他把话讲给招聘面试官，满足起点。
2.是否有条件特权（conditional privilege）：面试官在问，这类回答通常是为了第三人招聘利益，先进入特权。
3.特权是否被滥用（abuse）：
卡死点：若他对真伪有 substantial doubts，特权失效。
这时不再问“话题重不重要”，而是问他是不是明知不稳还继续说。
结论：若有严重怀疑 → 失去特权 → 可追责 → 选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然这句话是别人问出来的，而且还影响女方求职，应该就安全了。

但考试真正问的是：他当时有没有substantial doubts；有的话，特权就被打掉，不能拿“是对方先问的”当护身符。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干关键在于他对真伪若有 substantial doubts，就会把本来存在的条件特权打掉，所以女方可以赢。

❌ 事实误判 | 先问就安全

✕ A: 把inquired about当成免责任由，漏了特权还会被滥用。

❌ 法律适用 | 赔偿门槛错套

✕ B: 把pecuniary loss硬套进来，但这里是职业诋毁型 slander per se。

❌ 概念混淆 | 真假即赢

✕ C: 只盯false，忘了虚假只是起点，特权还可能挡住责任。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认“特权通信”，再看“有没有恶意怀疑”，不要被“对方先问”带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：条件特权（conditional privilege）先挡住责任，substantial doubts 再把特权打掉；问到“为了第三人利益说的”时，先查特权，再查滥用。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A senior member of the high school choir sued his music teacher for defamation based on the following facts: The director of a local choir called the teacher about the senior. The teacher, accidentally confusing the senior with another choir member with the same last name, stated that the senior was a bass. The senior was actually a tenor. The director did not contact the senior about joining the local choir because it needed more tenors, not basses.
Should the senior prevail in his lawsuit?

choices.A: No, because describing a person as a bass instead of a tenor is not a derogatory statement.
choices.B: No, because the senior cannot prove special damages in connection with the false statement.
choices.C: Yes, because the statement was false and the teacher was negligent in making it.
choices.D: Yes, because the teacher's false statement cost the senior a position in the local choir.

questions.explanation:
Defamatory statements harmful to plaintiff's reputation

Diminishing respect, esteem, or goodwill toward plaintiff
Deterring others from associating or dealing with plaintiff

Defamation can be either libel (written statements) or slander (spoken statements as seen here). A defamation claim based on slander requires proof of the following:

  • The defendant knowingly made a false statement about the plaintiff or negligently failed to determine its falsity.
  • The statement was defamatory, meaning that the type of statement would tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation.
  • The defendant intentionally or negligently communicated the statement to a third party.
  • The statement caused the plaintiff to suffer special damages or amounted to slander per se.

A statement is harmful to the plaintiff's reputation if it either diminishes respect, esteem, or goodwill toward the plaintiff OR deters others from associating with the plaintiff—e.g., had the teacher told the director that the senior had a poor work ethic. But since the teacher's statement that the senior was a bass instead of a tenor was not derogatory or harmful to his reputation in any way, the senior should not prevail in his defamation lawsuit.

(Choices B & D) Special damages require the plaintiff to prove that a third party heard the defendant's defamatory comments and acted adversely to the plaintiff. Most often, special damages involve an economic loss to the plaintiff, but they also would include such things as the director not contacting the senior about joining the local choir. In spite of this, the senior will not prevail because the teacher's statement was not defamatory.

(Choice C) The fact that the statement was false and that the teacher was negligent (ie, failed to use reasonable care) in making it is not a reason for the senior to prevail since the statement was not defamatory.

📌 Educational Objective

A statement is defamatory if the type of statement would tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation by diminishing respect, esteem, or goodwill toward the plaintiff OR deterring others from associating with the plaintiff.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 559 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (defamatory statement defined).
questions.zh-question:
一名高中合唱团的高年级成员以诽谤为由起诉其音乐老师，事实如下：当地一家合唱团的总监就该高年级成员的情况致电该老师。该老师意外地将该高年级成员与另一名同姓的合唱团成员混淆，并陈述该成员是男低音。而该高年级成员实际上是男高音。由于该合唱团需要的是男高音而非男低音，总监最终没有联系该高年级成员邀请其加入。

该高年级成员的诉讼应否胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为将一个人描述为男低音而非男高音并非贬损性陈述。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该高年级成员无法证明与该虚假陈述有关的特殊损害赔偿。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该陈述是虚假的，并且老师在做出该陈述时存在过失。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为老师的虚假陈述使该高年级成员失去了在当地合唱团中的一个位置。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Other Torts - Defamation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：一句看似“说错了”的话，是否真的属于诽谤（defamation）里会伤名誉的内容。

三秒认题路径：

说错了 → 传给第三人 → 会伤名誉？ → 不能成立

核心法律规则

诽谤（defamation）先看这句话有没有真正“贬损名誉”。考试意思：它必须让别人更看不起你，或不想再和你来往。诽谤口头陈述（slander）还要看是否对外传出、以及是否造成特殊损害（special damages）或属于slander per se。

但本题最关键的是：把学生说成男低音（bass），不是会毁名誉的侮辱；这只是声部搞错，不是对人格、品行或信誉的攻击。虚假（false）和过失（negligent）本身不够，得先有“会伤名誉”的内容。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 559 — 只有那种会降低他人尊重、敬意或好感，或让别人回避你，才算可诉的诽谤性陈述。

思维导图

先问：这句话有没有“伤名誉”属性？
NO：只是把人说成bass，不贬低品行、能力或信誉
卡死点：defamatory 这一关不过
YES：若是说你poor work ethic 这类会让人疏远的话，才继续看后续要件
结论：先过“会伤名誉”门槛，后面的虚假、传播、损害才有戏。
答案落点：不能成立

考点陷阱

你可能会想：老师说错了，还让合唱团主任没来找他，应该就能告。

但考试真正问的是：这句话本身是不是会让别人降低对他的尊重、敬意或好感。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里最容易被带偏的是把“有损失”直接等同于“有诽谤”；其实先看内容够不够贬损，special damages 只是后一步。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的bass vs. tenor 只是声部误认，不是贬损名誉的陈述；既然不构成诽谤，后面的损失再明显也救不回来。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ B: 把special damages 当成第一关了，顺序错。

❌ 法律适用 | 过失即成立

✕ C: 只盯着虚假和过失，忽略了先要“会伤名誉”。

❌ 事实误判 | 损失代替要件

✕ D: 见到没被联系就以为必胜，cost the senior 不能替代诽谤性。

这题建议用什么方法？

先筛“有没有贬损名誉”，再看传播和损害；别被后果带跑。

考场速记

记住：诽谤（defamation）先看“话是否真的贬名誉”，不是先看有没有损失。以后看到只是身份、声部、称呼搞错，就先怀疑defamatory 这一关没过。

C.text: false and the teacher was negligent

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
The owner of a truck leasing company asked one of his employees to deliver $1,000 to the dealership's main office. The following week, as a result of the owner's belief that the money had not been delivered, the owner instructed the employee to come to the office to submit to a lie detector test.
When the employee reported to the owner's office for the test, it was not administered. Instead, without hearing the employee's story, the owner shouted at him, "You're a thief!" and fired him. The owner's shout was overheard by several other employees who were in another office, which was separated from the owner's office by a thin partition. The next day, the employee accepted another job at a higher salary. Several weeks later, upon discovering that the money had not been stolen, the owner offered to rehire the employee.
In a suit for slander by the employee against the owner, will the employee prevail?

choices.A: No, because the statement was made to the employee alone and intended for his ears only.
choices.B: No, because the owner made the charge in good faith, believing it to be true.
choices.C: Yes, because the employee was fraudulently induced to go to the office for a lie detector test, which was not, in fact, given.
choices.D: Yes, because the owner should have foreseen that the statement would be overheard by other employees.

questions.explanation:
Defamation

(intentional or negligent communication requirement)
Intentionalcommunication
Negligentcommunication
Unforeseeablecommunication

Slander is defamation through speech, gesture, or any other form that is not libel. To prevail in a suit for slander, the plaintiff must prove all of the following:

  • The defendant knowingly made a false statement about the plaintiff or negligently failed to determine its falsity.
  • That type of statement would tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation.
  • The defendant intentionally or negligently communicated that statement to a third party (ie, should have foreseen that it would be heard by a third party).
  • That statement caused the plaintiff special harm (ie, pecuniary/monetary loss).

However, no proof of harm is required when the defamatory statement constitutes slander per se--ie, the statement accused the plaintiff of any of the following:

  • a serious crime (eg, theft, murder, rape)
  • conduct that adversely affects the plaintiff's occupation (eg, performing surgeries while intoxicated)
  • serious sexual misconduct (eg, infertility)
  • having a loathsome disease (eg, sexually transmitted infection).

Here, the owner falsely accused the employee of theft (slander per se). Since the owner made that statement without listening to the employee's story, the owner was likely negligent in failing to determine his statement was false. Additionally, though the accusation may have been intended for the employee's ears only, the owner should have foreseen that other employees would overhear him shouting through the thin partition (negligent communication) (Choice D). Therefore, the employee will likely prevail on his slander claim.

(Choice B) Slander requires proof that the defendant knew or negligently failed to determine that his/her statement was false. Here, although the owner believed in good faith that his accusation was true (no knowledge of falsity), he could still be liable for slander if he negligently failed to determine that his accusation was false.

(Choice C) Fraudulent inducement is an element of intentional misrepresentation, which requires proof that the defendant knowingly or recklessly misrepresented a material fact to induce the plaintiff's reliance. But since the employee only sued for slander, his fraudulent inducement is irrelevant.

📌 Educational Objective

Slander (ie, spoken defamation) requires proof that the defendant intentionally or negligently communicated a false statement about the plaintiff to a third party. Negligent communication occurs when the defendant should have foreseen that his/her statement would be heard by a third party.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 577 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (intentional or negligent communication).
questions.zh-question:
一家卡车租赁公司的老板要求其一名员工将1000美元送到经销商的主办公室。第二周，由于老板认为钱没有送到，他指示该员工到办公室接受测谎仪测试。

当该员工到老板办公室准备接受测试时，测试并未进行。相反，老板没有听该员工的解释，就对他大喊：“你是个小偷！”并解雇了他。老板的喊叫声被另一间办公室的几名员工听到，该办公室与老板的办公室仅由一堵薄薄的隔板隔开。第二天，该员工接受了另一份薪水更高的工作。几周后，当老板发现钱并未被盗时，他提出重新雇用该员工。

在该员工对老板提起的口头诽谤诉讼中，该员工会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该陈述是单独对该员工作出的，并且意图只让他一个人听到。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为老板是出于善意提出指控，相信其是真实的。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该员工被欺诈性地诱导到办公室进行测谎仪测试，而该测试实际上并未进行。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为老板应当预见到该陈述会被其他员工听到。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Other Torts - Defamation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：口头诽谤（slander）里，老板虽然是对员工本人骂，但只要他应当预见到会被第三人听见，就算“向第三人传播”成立。

三秒认题路径：

骂人定性 → 传给谁 → 能否预见 → 是否特权 → 选 D

核心法律规则

口头诽谤（slander）是用说话、手势或其他非书面方式实施的 诽谤（defamation），考场上先看这是不是“说出去的坏话”。

原告要赢，通常要证明：被告说的是假话或至少没有尽到核实义务；这句话会损害名誉；被告故意或过失地传播给第三人（intentional or negligent communication）；并造成损害。

第三人传播（communication to a third party）的考场意思：不一定要直接对旁人开口，should have foreseen 其他人会听到，也算传播到第三人。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 577 的思路锁定本题：只要应当预见会被第三人听见，传播要件就成立。

思维导图

老板当众说“你是小偷”
第1步：先看是不是 slander：口头骂人，不是书面。
第2步：这句话把员工说成 偷窃，属于 slander per se，不用另找金钱损失。
第3步：关键门槛不是“本来只想骂给他听”，而是有没有 negligent communication。
卡死点：薄隔板 + 其他员工在隔壁 = 应当预见会被听见。
结果：传播给第三人成立，员工可赢。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：老板是对着员工本人骂的，好像没有“讲给别人听”。

但考试真正问的是：他有没有 应当预见（should have foreseen） 隔壁同事会听见。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题的陷阱就是把“故意只想骂他”误当成“没有传播”；MBE 只要你能预见旁人会听到，就别被“只对他一个人说”骗走。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 thin partition 和隔壁员工在场，说明老板应当预见会被第三人听见；这就满足了 negligent communication。

❌ 概念混淆 | 只看受众误判

✕ A: 把“只想让他听见”误当成没有传播。

❌ 法律适用 | 善意抗辩误判

✕ B: 以为 good faith 就能挡住诽谤；只要没尽到核实义务，还是可能负责。

❌ 事实误判 | 偷换诉因焦点

✕ C: 把 lie detector 的事当成决定性事实；本题争点是诽谤传播，不是诱骗本身。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“有没有第三人听见”的传播要件，再看是否属于 slander per se。

考场速记

记住：slander 不要求一定“故意讲给旁人听”，只要你应当想到会被旁人听见，就够了。

看到“骂给一个人听、隔墙有人听到”这类题，先锁定 negligent communication，别被“本来只想骂他”带偏。

reason.en: Accusing the employee of theft is slander per se, satisfying the harm element.
reason.zh: 指控员工盗窃构成本身诽谤，满足损害要件。

reason.en: Makes it foreseeable that a shouted accusation would reach third parties.
reason.zh: 使大声指控可能被第三方听到具有可预见性。

reason.en: Shows the defamatory statement was communicated to third parties.
reason.zh: 表明诽谤性陈述已传达给第三方。

reason.en: Supports that the owner negligently failed to determine the statement was false.
reason.zh: 支持雇主过失地未查明陈述虚假。

reason.en: Identifies the cause of action and limits analysis to defamation elements.
reason.zh: 确定案由并将分析限定于诽谤构成要件。

reason.en: Background fact that does not supply a required slander element.
reason.zh: 背景事实，不构成口头诽谤所需要件。

reason.en: Ignores that foreseeable overhearing still publishes the statement to third parties.
reason.zh: 忽视可预见的偷听仍构成向第三方传播。

reason.en: Misstates slander law by treating private intent as defeating publication.
reason.zh: 误以私下意图否定向第三方传播要件。

reason.en: Good faith does not excuse negligent failure to determine falsity.
reason.zh: 善意不能免除过失查明虚假的责任。

reason.en: Distracts from negligence in verifying the accusation before shouting it.
reason.zh: 转移对 shouting 前未核实指控的过失关注。

reason.en: Raises a different tort not pleaded in this slander suit.
reason.zh: 提出本案未主张的另一侵权事由。

reason.en: Irrelevant to whether the slander elements are satisfied.
reason.zh: 与口头诽谤构成要件是否成立无关。

reason.en: States the correct negligent-communication standard for third-party hearing.
reason.zh: 表述第三方听到的正确过失传播标准。

reason.en: Directly satisfies the publication element required for slander.
reason.zh: 直接满足口头诽谤所需的传播要件。

highlights.text: You're a thief!

reason.en: A false charge of theft is slander per se, eliminating the need to prove special harm.
reason.zh: 虚假盗窃指控构成本身诽谤，无需证明特别损害。

highlights.text: overheard by several other employees

reason.en: Publication to third parties is required, and overhearing by coworkers satisfies it.
reason.zh: 口头诽谤需向第三方传播，被同事听到即满足该要件。

highlights.text: thin partition

reason.en: A thin partition makes it foreseeable that shouting would be heard next door.
reason.zh: 薄隔板使大声喊叫可能被隔壁听到具有可预见性。

highlights.text: without hearing the employee's story

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A hotel company owns and operates a beachfront hotel. Under a contract with the city to restore a public beach, a dredging company placed a large and unavoidably dangerous stone-crushing machine on the city's land near the hotel. The machine creates a continuous and intense noise that is so disturbing to the hotel guests that they have canceled their hotel reservations in large numbers, resulting in a substantial loss to the hotel company.
The hotel company's best chance to recover damages for its financial losses from the dredging company is under the theory that the operation of the stone-crushing machine constitutes which of the following?

choices.A: A private nuisance.
choices.B: A trespass.
choices.C: An abnormally dangerous activity.
choices.D: Negligence.

questions.explanation:
Damages for private nuisance
Compensatory
  • Property damage (eg, repair cost, depreciation)
  • Personal injury (eg, sickness, loss of consortium)
  • Emotional distress (requires personal injury in some jurisdictions)
  • Deprivation of use & enjoyment of property (ie, personal discomfort, inconvenience, annoyance)
  • Financial loss (eg, lost business)
Punitive
  • Available when interference was intentional, willful, or malicious

Liability for private nuisance arises when the defendant’s interference with the use and enjoyment of the plaintiff’s property is both:

  • substantial – offensive, annoying, or intolerable to a normal person in the community and
  • unreasonable – effectively renders the land unavailable for ordinary use or enjoyment by the possessor and satisfies certain criteria.

Once these elements are met, the plaintiff can recover damages for any type of harm caused by the interference—including financial loss (e.g., lost business).

Here, the dredging company interfered with the use and enjoyment of the hotel company’s property when it placed a stone-crushing machine that created a continuous and intense noise nearby. The interference was likely substantial since it caused many hotel guests to cancel their reservations. If that interference was also unreasonable—i.e., if it effectively rendered hotel property unavailable for guests to use and enjoy—then the hotel company could recover damages for its financial losses under the theory of private nuisance.

(Choice B) Trespass requires proof that the defendant intentionally entered the plaintiff’s property without his/her consent. Here, since the dredging company’s interference was caused by noise (not by an entry onto the hotel company’s property), the dredging company is not liable for trespass.

(Choice C) A defendant who engages in an abnormally dangerous activity is strictly liable (i.e., liable regardless of fault) for physical harm caused by a hazard that made the activity abnormally dangerous. Here, though the machine’s operation was unavoidably (and possibly abnormally) dangerous, the hotel company cannot recover under this theory since it only suffered financial loss—not physical harm (e.g., property damage, bodily harm).

(Choice D) The economic loss rule eliminates negligence liability for financial harm unaccompanied by physical harm. And since the hotel company is only seeking damages for financial harm—not physical harm such as property damage—it cannot recover under this theory.

📌 Educational Objective

Private nuisance—a substantial and unreasonable interference with the use and enjoyment of the plaintiff’s property—allows the plaintiff to recover damages for any type of harm, including financial loss.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Fourth) of Property § 2.1 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 3, 2022) (discussing the requirements of private nuisance).
  • Restatement (Fourth) of Property § 2.2 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 3, 2022) (defining what constitutes an unreasonable interference to establish a private nuisance).
questions.zh-question:
一家酒店公司拥有一家海滨酒店并负责其运营。根据与市政府签订的修复公共海滩的合同，一家疏浚公司在酒店附近的市政府土地上放置了一台大型且不可避免的危险碎石机。该机器产生持续且强烈的噪音，对酒店客人造成了极大的干扰，导致他们大量取消酒店预订，给酒店公司造成了重大损失。

该酒店公司向疏浚公司就其经济损失寻求损害赔偿的最佳诉因，是主张该碎石机的运营构成了以下哪项？

zh-choices.A: 私人妨害。
zh-choices.B: 非法侵入。
zh-choices.C: 异常危险活动。
zh-choices.D: 过失。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Other Torts - Nuisance

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：邻近噪音没有直接进入土地，也可能构成私人妨害（private nuisance），而且原告还能拿到财产相关损失（financial loss）赔偿。

三秒认题路径：

噪音干扰 → 不是侵入 → 看妨害 → 看是否重大且不合理 → 选 A

核心法律规则

私人妨害（private nuisance）考的是：被告对原告土地的使用与享受（use and enjoyment）造成了重大（substantial）且不合理（unreasonable）的干扰。考场意思：不是看你有没有碰到地，而是看你有没有把对方用地“吵到、烦到、用不了”。

一旦成立，原告可以拿赔偿，范围不只限于身体伤害，也可以包括财务损失（financial loss），比如生意流失。考场意思：妨害案里，损害类型没有被锁死在“地坏了”这一种。

本题里，石头粉碎机制造了持续、强烈噪音，导致大量住客取消预订，这正是把酒店的使用和经营实质打断了。

核心判例： Restatement (Fourth) of Property § 2.1 / § 2.2 — 说明私人妨害要看重大且不合理的干扰，而不是一定要有土地被踩进去。

思维导图

题干先给你什么？
事实触发邻海石料粉碎机 + 持续强噪音 + 住客大量退订 + 酒店财务损失
先排除什么？
不是 trespass没有“进入土地”，只是噪音影响，用错门类就会跑偏。
不是 abnormally dangerous activity这题只给财务损失，不是身体或财产的物理损害。
真正命中哪里？
private nuisance重大 + 不合理干扰使用与享受 → 可以追索financial loss
最后落点
答案选 A，因为噪音把酒店“用不顺”，不是把地“碰坏”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：没碰到酒店土地，所以不算侵权。但考试真正问的是：法律程序上和实体上能不能把“用地被严重干扰”当成妨害，而不是看有没有物理接触。

另一个坑是把“损失只是赚钱少了”误当成不能赔。其实私人妨害（private nuisance）本来就允许赔财务损失（financial loss），只要干扰够重大且不合理。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干持续强噪音让住客大量退订，说明对酒店使用和享受的干扰已经够重；私人妨害（private nuisance）正好能救financial loss。

❌ 概念混淆 | 进入要件误判

✕ B: 把noise当成土地被“进入”，其实这里只是干扰，不是侵入。

❌ 法律适用 | 物理伤害套错

✕ C: 看到abnormally dangerous就想套严格责任，但这题没给身体或财产损害。

❌ 事实误判 | 经济损失偷换

✕ D: 把economic loss rule拿来压妨害案，偷换成“只能赔物理伤害”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看干扰方式，再问是不是侵入；不是就转去妨害，看是否重大且不合理。

考场速记

记住一句：私人妨害（private nuisance）管的是“把你用地搞得不能好好用”，而且可以赔财务损失（financial loss）。下一次看到噪音、恶臭、烟尘先想妨害，不要先冲去 trespass。

reason.en: The machine was not placed on the hotel's property, ruling out trespass.
reason.zh: 机器不在酒店土地上，排除非法侵入。

reason.en: Off-site noise can still unreasonably interfere with guests' use and enjoyment.
reason.zh: 场外噪音仍可不合理干扰宾客对物业的使用与享用。

reason.en: Mass cancellations show the interference was substantial and harmed the hotel's business.
reason.zh: 大量取消预订表明干扰重大并损害酒店经营。

reason.en: Only private nuisance among the choices readily covers financial loss from property interference.
reason.zh: 在所列诉因中，仅私人妨害较能涵盖因物业干扰所致经济损失。

reason.en: Identifies the defendant's ongoing conduct causing the alleged interference.
reason.zh: 指明被告造成所谓干扰的持续行为来源。

reason.en: The plaintiff must hold a property interest subject to interference with use and enjoyment.
reason.zh: 原告须对受干扰使用与享用的物业享有财产利益。

reason.en: Covers substantial, unreasonable interference including recoverable financial loss.
reason.zh: 涵盖重大不合理干扰，包括可获赔偿的经济损失。

reason.en: Requires entry onto the plaintiff's land, not merely off-site noise.
reason.zh: 须实际进入原告土地，而非仅场外噪音。

label.zh: 异常危险活动严格责任

reason.en: Strict liability here is limited to physical harm, not pure financial loss.
reason.zh: 此严格责任限于人身或财产损害，不含纯粹经济损失。

reason.en: The economic loss rule bars negligence recovery for unaccompanied financial harm.
reason.zh: 经济损失规则禁止对无伴随物理损害之纯粹经济损失主张过失责任。

highlights.text: on the city's land near the hotel

reason.en: Shows the conduct occurred on adjacent city property, defeating trespass but not nuisance.
reason.zh: 表明行为发生在邻近市政土地上，排除非法侵入但不排除妨害。

highlights.text: continuous and intense noise

reason.en: Persistent offensive noise is the classic basis for a private nuisance claim.
reason.zh: 持续恼人噪音是私人妨害主张的典型基础。

highlights.text: recover damages for its financial losses

reason.en: The harm type determines which tort theories remain available.
reason.zh: 损害类型决定哪些侵权理论仍可适用。

highlights.text: canceled their hotel reservations in large numbers

reason.en: Widespread guest cancellations support that the interference was substantial.
reason.zh: 宾客大量取消预订支持干扰具有重大性。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
An assistant to a famous writer surreptitiously observed the writer as the writer typed her private password into her personal computer in order to access her email. On several subsequent occasions in the writer's absence, the assistant read the writer's email messages and printed out selections from them.
The assistant later quit his job and earned a considerable amount of money by leaking information to the media that he had learned from reading the writer's email messages. All of the information published about the writer as a result of the assistant's conduct was true and concerned matters of public interest.
The writer's secretary had seen the assistant reading the writer's emails and printing out selections, and she has told the writer what she saw. The writer now wishes to sue the assistant for damages. At trial, the writer can show that the media leaks could have come only from someone reading her email.
Can the writer recover damages from the assistant?

choices.A: No, because the assistant was an invitee on the premises.
choices.B: No, because the published information resulting from the assistant's conduct was true and concerned matters of public interest.
choices.C: Yes, because the assistant invaded the writer's privacy.
choices.D: Yes, because the published information resulting from the assistant's conduct constituted publication of private facts concerning the writer.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Invasion of privacy
Theories of recoveryRequired elements
Intrusion upon seclusion
  • Intentional intrusion (physical or otherwise) on plaintiff's solitude, seclusion, or private affairs
  • Intrusion would be highly offensive to reasonable person
Appropriation of name or likeness
  • Unauthorized use of plaintiff's name or likeness for personal benefit (typically for commercial purpose)
Public disclosure of private facts
  • Publicity given to plaintiff's private matter
  • Matter publicized would be both:
    • highly offensive to reasonable person
    • not of legitimate public concern
  • Results in damages
Publicity in a false light
  • Publicity given to false information that places plaintiff in false light
  • False light would be highly offensive to reasonable person
  • Publication is made with actual malice
  • Results in damages

Intrusion upon seclusion is an invasion of privacy that occurs when the defendant intentionally intrudes on the plaintiff's private affairs in a manner that would be highly offensive to a reasonable person-eg, tapping telephone wires, examining private bank account, opening personal mail.

Here, the assistant opened and read the writer's private, password-protected emails. Since a reasonable person would be highly offended by that intrusion, the writer can likely recover damages from the assistant for invasion of privacy (intrusion upon seclusion).

(Choice A) The fact that the assistant was an invitee shows that he had permission to enter the writer's premises, but does not show that he had permission to open and read the writer's private, password-protected emails. Therefore, the assistant's status as an invitee does not shield him from liability.

(Choice B) Truth is generally not a defense to invasion of privacy. And though public interest in the disclosed material may preclude an invasion of privacy claim based on public disclosure of private facts—publishing a private matter that is highly offensive and not of legitimate public concern—it is irrelevant to intrusion upon seclusion.

(Choice C) A privacy claim for the public disclosure of private facts requires proof that the publicized matter would be highly offensive to a reasonable person. Since there is no evidence that the writer's emails would be highly offensive, the writer cannot prevail on that claim.

(Choice D) A privacy claim for the public disclosure of private facts requires proof that the publicized matter would be highly offensive to a reasonable person. Since there is no evidence that the writer's emails would be highly offensive, the writer cannot prevail on that claim.

📌 Educational Objective

Intrusion upon seclusion (a type of invasion of privacy) occurs when the defendant intentionally intrudes on the plaintiff's private affairs in a manner that would be highly offensive to a reasonable person.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 652B (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (intrusion upon seclusion).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 652D (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (publicity given to private life).
questions.zh-question:
一位著名作家的助理，在该作家为了登录其电子邮件而将私人密码输入个人电脑时，偷偷地观察了她。在随后的几次，该助理趁作家不在时，阅读了作家的电子邮件并打印了其中的部分内容。

后来，该助理辞去了工作，并通过向媒体泄露他从阅读作家电子邮件中获知的信息，赚取了可观的收入。所有因此助理行为而发布的关于作家的信息都是真实的，并且涉及公共利益事项。

作家的秘书曾看到助理阅读作家的电子邮件并打印部分内容，她已将所见告知作家。作家现在希望起诉该助理以索取损害赔偿。在审判中，作家可以证明，媒体泄露的信息只可能来自阅读她电子邮件的人。

作家能否向该助理追讨损害赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为该助理是场所内的被邀请人。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为该助理行为所导致的已公布信息是真实的，并且涉及公共利益事项。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为该助理侵犯了作家的隐私权。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为该助理行为所导致的已公布信息构成了对作家私密事实的公布。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Other Torts - Invasion of privacy

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：侵入独处（intrusion upon seclusion），不是看发布内容真不真实，而是看他有没有偷偷闯入并读了你的私人邮箱。

三秒认题路径：

偷看邮箱 → 私密账号 → 故意闯入 → 很冒犯 → 选 Yes

核心法律规则

侵入独处（intrusion upon seclusion）的考场意思：被告故意闯进原告的私人事务（private affairs），而且这种闯入会让一般人觉得很冒犯。

这里不要求被告把内容公开出去；只要他偷偷进入、阅读、翻看原告的私密资料，责任就已经可能成立。

公共披露私人事实（public disclosure of private facts）要看“把私事公开给别人看”这一层，和本题的“偷偷读邮箱”不是一回事。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 652B — 这条规则直接锁定：偷偷读私人、密码保护的邮件，就是典型的 intrusion upon seclusion。

思维导图

先看被告做的是“偷偷闯入私人空间”还是“把私事公开出去”？
事实触发： 先偷看密码，再多次读邮件并打印内容
法律关卡： 故意侵入 私人事务（private affairs），是否会让一般人觉得很冒犯
卡死结论： 不必等到公开、也不必证明内容虚假；“真相 + 公共兴趣”卡不掉 intrusion
答案落点： 侵入独处已成立 → 原告可以索赔
排错提醒： 看到“媒体泄露是真实的”不要冲去选 public disclosure

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然最后被媒体知道了，而且内容都是真的、又和公共利益有关，那是不是就不能告了。

但考试真正问的是：被告前面有没有偷偷读你的私人邮件，这一步本身就已经是侵入独处。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的password-protected emails被反复偷读，正是 intrusion upon seclusion；不需要等公开或证明失实，原告就能要损害赔偿。

❌ 概念混淆 | 许可身份误判

✕ A: 把“能进门”当成“能看邮箱”，invitee 只管进入，不管偷读私信。

❌ 法律适用 | 真实性套错题

✕ B: 把“内容是真的”硬套进来，真相不挡住偷偷闯入私人邮箱。

❌ 事实误判 | 公开要件偷换

✕ D: 你把“后来被泄露”当成“本题要告公开事实”，但题干先问的是偷看邮件那一下。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓隐私侵入动作，再分清是“偷看”还是“公开”，不要被真伪和公共兴趣带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先问有没有偷闯私域，再问有没有公开内容。本题看到密码保护邮箱被偷读，第一反应就是 intrusion upon seclusion，不要先想 public disclosure。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Identify correct invasion of privacy theory

reason.en: Shows intentional, nonconsensual access to the writer's private conduct.
reason.zh: 表明故意、未经同意接触作家的私密行为。

reason.en: Signals that the email account was private and not open to the assistant.
reason.zh: 表明电子邮件账户属于私人领域，助理无权访问。

reason.en: Core conduct supporting intrusion upon seclusion.
reason.zh: 构成侵扰独处权的核心行为。

reason.en: Confirms deliberate exploitation of improperly accessed private communications.
reason.zh: 证明故意利用不当获取的私人通信。

keywords.text: true and concerned matters of public interest

reason.en: Distracts toward public disclosure of private facts, not intrusion.
reason.zh: 易误导至公开私人事实理论，而非侵扰独处。

reason.en: Frames the issue as whether any privacy tort supports damages.
reason.zh: 界定问题在于何种隐私侵权可支持赔偿。

reason.en: Misstates permission to enter as permission to read private emails.
reason.zh: 误将进入场所的许可视为查阅私人邮件的许可。

B.text: true and concerned matters of public interest

label.zh: 真实且具公共利益抗辩

reason.en: Applies to public disclosure of private facts, not intrusion upon seclusion.
reason.zh: 适用于公开私人事实，不适用于侵扰独处。

reason.en: Correctly identifies liability under intrusion upon seclusion.
